title.zh: 卷一百四十 列傳第六十五 崔苗二裴呂
title.en: Volume 140 Biographies 65: Cui Miao, two Pei's, Lu
title.raw: 卷一百四十 列傳第六十五 崔苗二裴呂 Volume 140 Biographies 65: Cui Miao, two Pei's, Lu

sentences.zh: 崔苗二裴呂

translations.literal: Cui, Miao, the two Peis, and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Cui, Miao, the two Peis, and Lu.

translations.literal: 4.1.1 Pei Shu.
translations.idiomatic: 4.1.1 Pei Shu.

sentences.zh: 崔圓，字有裕，貝州武城人，後魏尚書左仆射亮八世孫。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan, styled Youyu, was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou, eighth-generation descendant of Liang, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan, courtesy name Youyu, came from Wucheng in Beizhou and was the eighth-generation descendant of Liang, who had served as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，志向卓邁，喜學兵家。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor; his aspirations were lofty, and he delighted in studying military strategists.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in his youth, he harbored lofty ambitions and took pleasure in studying the art of war.

sentences.zh: 開元中，詔舉遺逸，以鈐謀對策甲科，歷京兆府參軍，尹蕭炅薦之，遷會昌丞。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era an edict summoned recluses of outstanding talent; he answered on military strategy in the first class, served as an aide in the Jingzhao prefecture, was recommended by Prefect Xiao Jiong, and was promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign an edict called up recluses of outstanding talent; Yuan passed the military-strategy examination in the top grade, served as an aide in the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture, was recommended by the prefect Xiao Jiong, and was promoted to assistant magistrate of Huichang.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠遙領劍南節度，引圓為左司馬，知留後。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong held the Jiannan military commission in absentia and brought Yuan in as Left Major, with charge of the rear administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong held the Jiannan commission in name only, he brought Yuan in as left major and put him in charge of the rear administration.

sentences.zh: 玄宗西出，次撫風，遷御史中丞、劍南節度副大使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong marched west and halted at Fufeng, Yuan was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and Vice Commissioner of the Jiannan military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong fled west and paused at Fufeng, Yuan was promoted to censor-in-chief and deputy commissioner of the Jiannan military commission.

sentences.zh: 圓銳功名，初聞難，刺國忠意，乃治城浚隍，列館宇，儲什具。

translations.literal: Yuan was keen for achievement and fame; when he first heard of the crisis he divined Guozhong's intent and thereupon repaired the walls, deepened the moats, arranged lodging houses, and stockpiled supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious for fame and advancement, Yuan took the first news of disaster as a cue to Yang Guozhong's intentions; he fortified the city, deepened the moats, set up lodging, and laid in stores of every kind.

sentences.zh: 帝次河池，圓疏具陳「蜀土腴穀羨，儲供易辦」。

translations.literal: When the emperor halted at Hechi, Yuan submitted a memorial fully stating that "the soil of Shu is rich and grain abundant; provisions are easy to prepare."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor stopped at Hechi, Yuan submitted a detailed memorial arguing that Shu was fertile and grain-rich, and that supplies there would be easy to arrange.

sentences.zh: 帝省書泣下曰：「世亂識忠臣。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and wept, saying: "In troubled times one knows loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and wept, saying, "In times of chaos one learns who the loyal ministers are.

sentences.zh: 」即日拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，仍兼劍南節度使。

translations.literal: " That very day he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery, while still retaining the Jiannan military commission.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day Yuan was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Chancellery, while continuing to hold the Jiannan military commission.

sentences.zh: 天子至，朝廷百司殿宇帷幔皆具，益嗟賞之。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven arrived, the halls, offices, and hangings of the court were all in readiness, and he admired Yuan all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived, the halls of government and their furnishings were all ready, and his admiration for Yuan only grew.

sentences.zh: 肅宗立，命與房琯、韋見素赴行在所，帝為製遺愛碑於蜀以寵之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong was established, he ordered Yuan to go with Fang Guan and Wei Jiansu to the traveling court; the emperor had a stele of enduring affection erected in Shu to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Suzong took the throne, Yuan was ordered to join Fang Guan and Wei Jiansu at the mobile court; the former emperor had a stele of enduring affection set up in Shu to honor him.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，遷中書令，封趙國公，實封戶五百。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, with five hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhide era he was promoted to director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with a substantive fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，罷為太子少師，留守東都。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan he was removed and made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with charge as defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan he was dismissed to the post of junior tutor to the heir apparent and left to guard the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 於是上皇所置宰相無在者。

translations.literal: Thus none of the chancellors the Retired Emperor had appointed remained in office.
translations.idiomatic: By then none of the chancellors the retired emperor had appointed still held office.

sentences.zh: 王師之敗相州也，軍所過，皆縱剽，圓懼，委東都，奔襄陽，詔削階、封。

translations.literal: When the imperial army was defeated at Xiangzhou, wherever the troops passed they plundered at will; Yuan was afraid, abandoned the Eastern Capital, and fled to Xiangyang; an edict stripped his rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial army's defeat at Xiangzhou, the troops looted wherever they marched; fearing for himself, Yuan abandoned the Eastern Capital and fled to Xiangyang, and an edict stripped him of rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 尋召拜濟王傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Tutor to the Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and appointed tutor to the Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 李光弼表為懷州刺史，改汾州，以治行稱。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi memorialized to appoint him Prefect of Huaizhou; he was transferred to Fenzhou and was praised for his conduct in office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi recommended him for prefect of Huaizhou; he was later moved to Fenzhou, where his administration won renown.

sentences.zh: 徙淮南節度使，在鎮六年，請朝京師，吏民乞留，詔檢校尚書右仆射，還之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Huainan; after six years in the post he requested audience at the capital; officials and people begged him to stay; an edict made him Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of Huainan; after six years in the region he asked to attend court at the capital, but officials and commoners pleaded that he stay, so an edict named him acting right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 久乃檢校左仆射，入知省事。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was made Acting Left Vice Director and entered to oversee Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Only after some time was he made acting left vice director and brought in to handle Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 大歷中卒，年六十四，贈太子太師，謚曰昭襄。

translations.literal: He died in the Dali era, aged sixty-four; posthumously he was given Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with posthumous title Zhaoxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Dali era at the age of sixty-four and was posthumously honored as grand tutor to the heir apparent with the temple name Zhaoxiang.

sentences.zh: 苗晉卿

translations.literal: Miao Jinqing.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jinqing.

sentences.zh: 苗晉卿，字元輔，潞州壺關人，世以儒素稱。

translations.literal: Miao Jinqing, styled Yuanfu, was a native of Huguan in Luzhou; for generations his family was known for Confucian plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jinqing, courtesy name Yuanfu, was from Huguan in Luzhou; his family had long been known for scholarly simplicity.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，調為修武尉，累進吏部郎中、中書舍人，知吏部選事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Wei of Xiuwu, and rose through posts as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Drafting Secretary, with charge of personnel selection.
translations.idiomatic: After taking the jinshi degree he was appointed magistrate of Xiuwu and rose through the Ministry of Personnel to drafting secretary, with responsibility for civil-service selection.

sentences.zh: 選人訴索好官，厲言倨色紛於前，晉卿與相對，終日無慍顏。

translations.literal: Candidates for office pleaded and demanded good posts; harsh words and arrogant faces pressed before him, yet Jinqing faced them all day without a trace of anger.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates clamored for desirable posts, heaping harsh words and arrogant demands upon him, yet Jinqing faced them from morning to night without showing irritation.

sentences.zh: 久之，進侍郎，積寬縱，而吏下因緣作奸。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Vice Director; he grew ever more lenient and indulgent, and subordinate clerks took advantage to commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to vice director; his indulgence deepened, and the clerks beneath him seized the chance for corruption.

sentences.zh: 方時承平，選常萬人，李林甫為尚書，專國政，以銓事委晉卿及宋遙，然歲命它官同較書判，核才實。

translations.literal: At that time, in an age of peace, selections often ran to ten thousand men; Li Linfu was Director and monopolized state affairs, entrusting evaluation to Jinqing and Song Yao, yet each year other officials were ordered to join in comparing documents and judgments to verify talent and fact.
translations.idiomatic: In those peaceful years selections often involved ten thousand candidates; Li Linfu, as director of the ministry, controlled the government and left the evaluations to Jinqing and Song Yao, but each year other officials were also assigned to review the papers and test candidates' real ability.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年，判入等者凡六十四人，分甲、乙、丙三科，以張奭為第一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao, those judged to have passed numbered sixty-four in all, divided into three grades of jia, yi, and bing; Zhang Shi was placed first.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianbao sixty-four candidates were judged to have passed, ranked in three grades; Zhang Shi was placed first.

sentences.zh: 奭，御史中丞倚之子，倚新得幸於帝，晉卿欲附之，奭本無學，故議者囂然不平。

translations.literal: Shi was the son of Censor-in-Chief Yi; Yi had newly won the emperor's favor, and Jinqing wished to attach himself to him; Shi was utterly without learning, so critics were loudly indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was the son of Censor-in-Chief Yi, who had lately won the emperor's favor; Jinqing sought to curry favor with the father, but Shi had no learning to speak of, and public opinion seethed with outrage.

sentences.zh: 安祿山因間言之，帝為禦花萼樓覆實，中裁十一二，奭持紙終日，筆不下，人謂之「曳白」。

translations.literal: An Lushan seized the moment to speak of it; the emperor went to the Hua'e Tower to verify in person; of those re-examined only one or two in ten passed; Shi held the paper all day without setting brush to it—people called it "dragging the blank."
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan brought the matter to the emperor's attention; the emperor went to the Hua'e Tower to verify the results in person; only one or two in ten of those re-tested passed; Shi held his examination paper all day without writing a word, and people dubbed it "dragging a blank sheet."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，貶倚淮陽太守，遙武當太守，晉卿安康太守。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged; Yi was demoted to Prefect of Huaiyang, Yao to Prefect of Wudang, and Jinqing to Prefect of Ankang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious: Yi was demoted to prefect of Huaiyang, Yao to prefect of Wudang, and Jinqing to prefect of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙魏郡，即充河北采訪使。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Weijun and at once made Hebei Investigating Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was moved to Weijun and appointed investigating commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 居三年，政化大行。

translations.literal: After three years in the post, his governance and transforming influence were widely felt.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office his reforms had taken deep hold.

sentences.zh: 嘗入計，謁歸壺關，望縣門輒步，吏諫止，晉卿以「公門當下，況父母邦乎」？

translations.literal: Once when he entered the capital on account, he returned to pay respects at Huguan; seeing the county gate he would walk; clerks remonstrated and stopped him; Jinqing said, "Before the public gate one should dismount—how much more in one's parents' homeland?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, coming to the capital on official business, he returned to pay respects in Huguan; at sight of the county gate he would dismount and walk, and when clerks tried to stop him he said, "One should walk before the public gate—how much more in one's native district?"

sentences.zh: 郡太守迎犒，使所屬令行酒，酒至，必立飲白釂，侍老有獻，降西階拜而飲，時美其恭。

translations.literal: The prefect welcomed and feasted him, had the county magistrate under his command pass the wine; when wine came he always stood, drank it dry in one cup; when elders offered cups he descended the west steps, bowed, and drank; contemporaries praised his reverence.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect welcomed him with a feast and had the local magistrate pass the wine; whenever a cup reached him he stood and drained it in one; when elders offered wine he went down the west steps, bowed, and drank; people at the time admired his deference.

sentences.zh: 改河東郡，兼河東采訪使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hedong commandery and concurrently made Hedong Investigating Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hedong commandery and concurrently made investigating commissioner for Hedong.

sentences.zh: 徙撫風郡，封高平縣男。

translations.literal: He was moved to Fufeng commandery and enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoping county.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Fufeng commandery and enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書、東都留守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Works and Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of works and defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 召為憲部，兼左丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the Ministry of Justice and concurrently made Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the Ministry of Justice and concurrently made left assistant director.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，竇廷芝棄陜郡不守，楊國忠本忌其有望，即奏「東道賊沖，非大臣不可鎮遏」，授陜郡太守、陜虢防禦使，晉卿見帝，以老辭，忤旨，聽致仕於家。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Dou Tingzhi abandoned Shaan commandery without defending it; Yang Guozhong had long resented Jinqing's prospects and at once memorialized that "the eastern route is struck by rebels and only a great minister can hold them in check," appointing him Prefect of Shaan and Defense Commissioner of Shan-Guo; Jinqing saw the emperor and declined on grounds of age, offended the imperial will, and was permitted to retire at home.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Dou Tingzhi abandoned Shaan commandery without a fight; Yang Guozhong, who had long envied Jinqing's standing, immediately memorialized that the eastern route was overrun and only a senior minister could contain the rebels, and appointed him prefect of Shaan and defense commissioner of Shan-Guo; Jinqing appeared before the emperor, pleaded old age, offended the throne, and was allowed to retire at home.

sentences.zh: 車駕入蜀，搢紳多陷賊，晉卿間道走金州。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage entered Shu, many gentry fell into the rebels' hands; Jinqing took bypaths and fled to Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled into Shu, many officials were trapped by the rebels; Jinqing escaped by back roads to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉卿寬厚，所至以惠化稱。

translations.literal: Jinqing was generous and magnanimous; wherever he went he was praised for benevolent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was generous and mild; wherever he served he was known for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 魏人為營生祠，立石頌美。

translations.literal: The people of Wei built him a living shrine and erected a stone to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei built him a living shrine and set up a stone inscription in his praise.

sentences.zh: 再秉政，出入七年，小心謹畏，不甚斥是非得失，故能安保寵名。

translations.literal: Twice he held the reins of government, coming and going over seven years; cautious and fearful, he did not much denounce right and wrong or gain and loss, and so was able to keep his favor and name secure.
translations.idiomatic: He held high office twice over seven years in all; careful and restrained, he rarely spoke out on rights and wrongs, and thus preserved both favor and reputation.

sentences.zh: 然練達事體，百官簿最，一省無遺，議者比漢胡廣。

translations.literal: Yet he was thoroughly versed in the substance of affairs; the registers of the hundred offices—he surveyed them without omission; critics compared him to Hu Guang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was thoroughly versed in administrative detail; the records of every office lay open to him at a glance, and commentators compared him to Hu Guang of the Han.

sentences.zh: 肅宗欲以李輔國為常侍，奏曰：「常侍近密，非賢不可居，豈宜任等輩？

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong wished to appoint Li Fuguo as Palace Attendant; Jinqing memorialized: "The Palace Attendant is close and intimate; only the worthy may hold it—how can such a man be appointed?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong wished to make Li Fuguo a palace attendant, Jinqing memorialized, "That post is close to the throne and demands a man of talent—how can someone of his sort hold it?"

sentences.zh: 」罷之。

translations.literal: " The appointment was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲論陳希烈等死，晉卿曰：「陛下得張通儒、安守忠、孫孝哲等，何以加罪？

translations.literal: The court wished to debate putting Chen Xilie and others to death; Jinqing said: "Your Majesty has Zhang Tongru, An Shouzhong, Sun Xiaozhe, and the like—how can you add further punishments?"
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated executing Chen Xilie and others, Jinqing said, "Your Majesty already holds Zhang Tongru, An Shouzhong, Sun Xiaozhe, and the like—how can you pile on more punishments?"

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 俄而史思明亂，持是以誘眾。

translations.literal: Before long Shi Siming rebelled and used this very point to win followers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shi Siming rebelled and used this very argument to win men to his side.

sentences.zh: 嘗自為父碑文，有鵲巢碑上。

translations.literal: Once he himself composed an inscription for his father's tomb; a magpie nested on the stele.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote an inscription for his father's tomb, and a magpie nested on the stone.

sentences.zh: 賊入上黨，焚蕩略盡，而苗氏松槚獨無傷。

translations.literal: When rebels entered Shangdang they burned and ravaged nearly everything, yet the pines and cypresses of the Miao clan alone were unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels entered Shangdang they burned and ravaged almost everything, yet the pines at the Miao family graves alone were untouched.

sentences.zh: 大歷七年，配享肅宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali he was given paired sacrifice in Emperor Suzong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dali he was granted a place in the sacrifices at Emperor Suzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 十子：發、丕、堅、粲、垂、向、呂、稷、望、咸。

translations.literal: He had ten sons: Fa, Pi, Jian, Can, Chui, Xiang, Lü, Ji, Wang, and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons: Fa, Pi, Jian, Can, Chui, Xiang, Lü, Ji, Wang, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 粲，德宗時官至郎中，陸贄欲進粲官，帝不許，曰：「晉卿往攝政，有不臣之言。

translations.literal: Can, in Emperor Dezong's time, reached the post of Director; Lu Zhi wished to promote Can in rank, but the emperor would not allow it, saying: "When Jinqing formerly held regency there were disloyal words.
translations.idiomatic: Can rose to director under Emperor Dezong; Lu Zhi wished to promote him, but the emperor refused, saying, "When Jinqing once held regency he spoke words unbecoming a subject.

sentences.zh: 又名其子，皆與帝王同，粲等宜與外官。

translations.literal: He also named his sons with characters shared with emperors; Can and the rest should receive only outer-circle offices."
translations.idiomatic: He even gave his sons names that echoed imperial usage; Can and his brothers should receive only peripheral appointments."

sentences.zh: 」贄奏：「王者爵人必於朝，刑人必於市，言與眾共之。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized: "A king ennobles men only in court and punishes men only in the marketplace—meaning that he shares the matter with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied in a memorial, "A true king ennobles men only in court and punishes them only in the marketplace, because he shares such decisions with the people.

sentences.zh: 獎而不言其善，斯謂曲貸；

translations.literal: To reward without stating the good is what is called crooked favor;
translations.idiomatic: To reward without stating the merit is crooked favor;

sentences.zh: 罰而不書其惡，斯謂中傷。

translations.literal: to punish without recording the evil is what is called slanderous injury.
translations.idiomatic: to punish without recording the fault is slander by omission.

sentences.zh: 曲貸，則授受不明，而私幸之門啟；

translations.literal: Crooked favor makes granting and receiving unclear and opens the gate of private favor;
translations.idiomatic: Crooked favor blurs who gives and who receives and opens the door to private patronage;

sentences.zh: 中傷，則枉直無辨，而讒間之道行。

translations.literal: slanderous injury leaves crooked and straight undistinguished and sets the way of malicious division in motion.
translations.idiomatic: slander by omission leaves right and wrong undistinguished and lets calumny flourish.

sentences.zh: 可不慎哉！

translations.literal: Can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Can Your Majesty not be cautious in this?

sentences.zh: 若陛下以晉卿奸邪，粲等應坐，則當公議其罪；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty holds that Jinqing was treacherous and evil and that Can and the rest should be implicated, then their crimes should be debated in public;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty believes Jinqing was treacherous and that Can and his brothers should share the guilt, then their crimes ought to be debated openly;

sentences.zh: 若知見誣，亦宜擢粲等以示天下。

translations.literal: if you know they were slandered, you should also promote Can and the rest to show the empire.
translations.idiomatic: if you know they were slandered, you should promote Can and his brothers to show the empire where you stand.

sentences.zh: 且晉卿起文儒，致位臺輔，謙柔敦厚，為三朝所推，安肯為族滅計？

translations.literal: Moreover Jinqing rose from literary Confucianism to the highest offices; humble, gentle, and sincere, he was commended by three reigns—how would he consent to a plan that exterminated his clan?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Jinqing rose from the world of letters to the highest office; humble, gentle, and sincere, he was trusted through three reigns—why would he ever plot the destruction of his own house?

sentences.zh: 雖甚狂險猶不為之，況老臣乎？

translations.literal: Even the most wildly reckless would not do such a thing—how much less an old minister?
translations.idiomatic: Even the wildest and most reckless man would not do such a thing—how much less a veteran minister?

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，而粲官終不顯。

translations.literal: " The emperor agreed, yet Can's office never rose to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor assented, yet Can never attained high rank.

sentences.zh: 裴冕，字章甫，河中河東人，本冠族仕家，以蔭再調渭南尉。

translations.literal: Pei Mian, styled Zhangfu, was a native of Hedong in Hezhong; his family was originally of eminent clan and official house; through yin privilege he was twice appointed Wei of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian, courtesy name Zhangfu, was from Hedong in Hezhong; his family was of distinguished official lineage, and through yin privilege he was twice appointed magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 王鉷為京畿采訪使，表署判官，歷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Wang Hong was Investigating Commissioner of the Capital Region and memorialized to appoint him as administrative aide; he served as Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hong was investigating commissioner for the capital region he had Mian appointed as his aide; Mian later served as palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 冕少學術，然明銳，果於事，眾呈稱職，鉷雅任之。

translations.literal: Mian in youth studied the classics, yet he was sharp and keen, resolute in affairs; the crowd all said he fulfilled his duties, and Hong greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Mian had studied the classics in his youth, but he was sharp and decisive in action; everyone said he did his job well, and Hong relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 及鉷得罪，有詔廷辨，冕位甚下，而抗言其誣。

translations.literal: When Hong fell into guilt there was an edict for court debate; Mian's rank was very low, yet he spoke out boldly that Hong had been slandered.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong was accused, an edict ordered a court debate; though Mian's rank was low, he spoke up boldly that Hong had been framed.

sentences.zh: 鉷死，李林甫方用事，僚屬懼，皆引去，獨冕為斂葬，由是浸知名。

translations.literal: When Hong died, Li Linfu was just then in power; his subordinates were afraid and all withdrew; Mian alone arranged the burial, and from this gradually became known.
translations.idiomatic: After Hong died, with Li Linfu in power his former subordinates fled in fear; Mian alone arranged the burial, and from that time his name slowly spread.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使哥舒翰辟行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Geshu Han, military commissioner of Hexi, recruited him as Marching Major.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, military commissioner of Hexi, recruited him as marching major.

sentences.zh: 玄宗入蜀，詔皇太子為天下兵馬元帥，拜冕御史中丞兼左庶子副之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong entered Shu, an edict made the Crown Prince Commander-in-Chief of all armies; Mian was appointed Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Left Subordinate of the Heir to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong fled into Shu, an edict named the crown prince commander-in-chief of all armies and appointed Mian censor-in-chief and left subordinate of the heir to assist him.

sentences.zh: 初，冕在河西，方召還，而道遇太子平涼，遂從至靈武，與杜鴻漸、崔漪同辭進曰：「主上厭於勤，且南狩蜀，宗社神器，要須有歸。

translations.literal: At first Mian was in Hexi and had just been summoned back when on the road he met the Crown Prince at Pingliang; he followed on to Lingwu and, with Du Hongjian and Cui Yi, together advanced in memorial: "The sovereign is weary of toil and has gone south to hunt in Shu; the altars of state and the imperial regalia must find their resting place.
translations.idiomatic: Mian had been in Hexi and was on his way back when he met the crown prince at Pingliang; he followed him to Lingwu and, with Du Hongjian and Cui Yi, jointly urged, "The emperor is weary of rule and has gone south into Shu; the altars of state and the imperial regalia must find a home.

sentences.zh: 今天意人事，屬在殿下，宜正位號。

translations.literal: Now Heaven's intent and human affairs belong to Your Highness; you should rectify the title and throne."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent and the people's will now rest with Your Highness; you should take the throne."

sentences.zh: 有如逡巡，失億兆心，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: If there is hesitation and the hearts of the hundred millions are lost, then the great enterprise is gone.
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate and lose the hearts of the people, the great cause will be lost.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「我平寇逆，奉迎乘輿還京師，退居涼貳，以侍膳左右，豈不樂哉！

translations.literal: The Crown Prince said: "I shall pacify the rebels and bandits, welcome the imperial carriage back to the capital, withdraw to a cool second place, and attend at meals left and right—would that not be joy enough!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "I mean to crush the rebels, welcome the emperor back to the capital, and withdraw to a secondary role, attending him at table—what could be happier than that!

sentences.zh: 公等何言之過！

translations.literal: Why do you gentlemen speak so excessively!"
translations.idiomatic: Why do you speak so extravagantly!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「殿下居東宮二十年，今多難啟聖，以安社稷，而所從將士皆關輔人，日夜思歸，大眾一騷，不可復集，不如因而撫之，以就大功。

translations.literal: They replied: "Your Highness dwelt in the Eastern Palace twenty years; now in many calamities you are called to sagehood to settle the altars; yet the officers and soldiers who follow you are all men of Guanfu, thinking day and night of returning home; if the great host is once stirred, it cannot be gathered again—better to take advantage and reassure them to accomplish the great deed.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Your Highness has been heir for twenty years; now in this time of calamity you are called to save the realm. Yet the soldiers who follow you are all men of the capital region, longing day and night to go home; once the army is unsettled it cannot be rallied again. Better to win them over now and achieve the great work.

sentences.zh: 臣等昧死請。

translations.literal: We your servants beg at the risk of death."
translations.idiomatic: We beg this at the risk of our lives."

sentences.zh: 」太子固讓，凡五請，卒見聽。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince firmly declined; in all he was petitioned five times and finally was persuaded.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince refused firmly; they pleaded five times before he at last consented.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，進冕中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince took the throne, Mian was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince took the throne, Mian was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 乃建言賣官、度僧道士，收貲濟軍興。

translations.literal: He thereupon proposed selling offices and ordaining monks and Daoist priests, collecting fees to supply military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed selling offices and ordaining monks and Daoist priests, using the proceeds to fund the armies.

sentences.zh: 時取償既賤，眾不為宜。

translations.literal: At the time the fees taken were so cheap that the multitude thought it unfitting.
translations.idiomatic: The fees demanded were so low that many thought the policy improper.

sentences.zh: 肅宗至鳳翔，罷冕政事，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong reached Fengxiang, Mian was removed from government affairs and appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong reached Fengxiang, Mian was removed from active government and made right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，封冀國公，實封五百戶，出為劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with a substantive fief of five hundred households and sent out as military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with a substantive fief of five hundred households and sent out as military commissioner of western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 復為右僕射，待制集賢院。

translations.literal: He was again made Right Vice Director and Attendant Drafting at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made right vice director and attendant drafting at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 俄充山陵使。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Commissioner for the Imperial Tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed commissioner for the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 於是，中書舍人劉烜為李輔國所昵，冕表為判官。

translations.literal: At this time Drafting Secretary Liu Xuan was favored by Li Fuguo; Mian memorialized to appoint him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the drafting secretary Liu Xuan was a favorite of Li Fuguo; Mian recommended him as his administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 烜抵法，坐降施州刺史，徙澧州。

translations.literal: Xuan violated the law and was demoted to Prefect of Shi, then transferred to Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan ran afoul of the law, Mian was demoted to prefect of Shi and then moved to Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，郭子儀言於代宗曰：「冕首佐先帝，馳驅靈武，有社稷勛，程元振忌其賢，遂加誣構，海內冤之。

translations.literal: In the Dali era Guo Ziyi spoke to Emperor Daizong: "Mian was the first to assist the late emperor, riding in haste to Lingwu; he had merit for the altars of state; Cheng Yuanzhen envied his worth and thereupon slandered and framed him—the empire found it unjust."
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era Guo Ziyi told Emperor Daizong, "Mian was among the first to support the late emperor, riding hard to Lingwu; he earned merit for the realm. Cheng Yuanzhen envied his talent and framed him, and the whole empire regarded it as an injustice."

sentences.zh: 陛下宜還冕於朝，復俾輔相，必能致治成化。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should return Mian to court and again make him a chief minister; he will surely bring order and complete transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should bring Mian back to court and restore him as chief minister; he will surely help restore good government.

sentences.zh: 」時元載秉政，冕早所甄引，載德之，又貪其衰瘵，且下己，遂拜左僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zai held the government; Mian had long ago been the one who selected and promoted him; Zai was grateful and also coveted his weakness and infirmity, and that he was beneath himself—thereupon Mian was appointed Left Vice Director and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai then held power; Mian had long ago been the man who advanced him, and Zai was grateful, but he also counted on Mian's age and infirmity and on being his superior—so Mian was appointed left vice director and associate director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 入見，拜不能興，載自扶之，代為贊謝。

translations.literal: On entering audience he could not rise in bow; Zai himself supported him and answered thanks in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to audience he could not rise to bow; Zai himself helped him up and answered the emperor's thanks on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 俄兼河南江淮副元帥、東都留守。

translations.literal: Before long he was concurrently made Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Henan and the Jiang-Huai region and Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made deputy commander-in-chief for Henan and the Jiang-Huai region and defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 不逾月卒，有詔贈太尉。

translations.literal: In less than a month he died; an edict posthumously gave him Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he died; an edict posthumously honored him as grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 冕以忠勤自將，然不知宰相大體。

translations.literal: Mian conducted himself with loyalty and diligence, yet he did not understand the great principles of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Mian led with loyalty and diligence, yet he did not grasp the larger duties of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 性豪侈，既素貴，輿服食飲皆光麗珍豐，櫪馬直數百金者常十數，每廣會賓客，不能名其饌，自製巾子工甚，人爭效之，號「僕射巾」。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant; having long been noble, his carriages, food, clothing, and drink were all lustrous, fine, and abundant; horses in his stable worth several hundred cash each numbered regularly in the tens; whenever he gave broad feasts for guests he could not name the dishes; the headcloth he designed himself was very skillfully made—people vied to imitate it, and it was called the "Vice Director's cap."
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was lavish; born to high rank, his carriages, dress, food, and drink were all splendid and costly; he routinely kept a dozen horses in his stable worth several hundred strings of cash each; at his grand banquets he could not even name every dish served; the headcloth he designed was so finely made that people rushed to copy it, and it was nicknamed the "Vice Director's cap."

sentences.zh: 領使既眾，吏白俸簿月二千緡，冕顧視，喜見顏間，世訾其嗜利云。

translations.literal: His commissionerships were many; a clerk reported that the salary register came to two thousand strings of cash per month; Mian looked it over and delight showed on his face—later ages reviled his love of profit.
translations.idiomatic: He held so many commissions that a clerk reported his monthly salary register at two thousand strings of cash; Mian looked it over with visible pleasure, and later generations condemned his greed.

sentences.zh: 始，肅宗廟惟苗晉卿配享，冕卒後二十餘年，有蘇正元者奏言：「肅宗為元帥時，師才一旅，冕於草創中，甄大義以勸進，收募驍勇幾十餘萬。

translations.literal: At first in Emperor Suzong's temple only Miao Jinqing received paired sacrifice; more than twenty years after Mian's death a man named Su Zhengyuan memorialized: "When Suzong was Commander-in-Chief his army was but one brigade; Mian in the founding days discerned the great principle and urged advancement, gathering and recruiting fierce warriors to nearly a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At first only Miao Jinqing shared sacrifice in Emperor Suzong's temple; more than twenty years after Mian's death a man named Su Zhengyuan memorialized, "When Suzong was commander-in-chief his forces numbered barely a brigade; Mian, in those founding days, grasped the larger cause and urged him to take the throne, raising nearly a hundred thousand fierce troops.

sentences.zh: 既逾月，房琯來；

translations.literal: After more than a month Fang Guan came;
translations.idiomatic: More than a month passed before Fang Guan arrived;

sentences.zh: 又一年，而晉卿至。

translations.literal: another year passed and Jinqing arrived.
translations.idiomatic: and another year passed before Jinqing came.

sentences.zh: 今晉卿從祀，而冕乃不與。

translations.literal: Now Jinqing follows in sacrifice, yet Mian is not included.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing now shares the sacrifices, yet Mian does not.

sentences.zh: 」有詔冕配享肅宗廟。

translations.literal: " An edict granted Mian paired sacrifice in Emperor Suzong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict then granted Mian a place in the sacrifices at Emperor Suzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 裴遵慶

translations.literal: Pei Zunqing.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zunqing.

sentences.zh: 裴遵慶，字少良，絳州聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Zunqing, styled Shaoliang, was a native of Wenxi in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zunqing, courtesy name Shaoliang, was from Wenxi in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼強學，該綜圖傳，外晦內明，不幹當世。

translations.literal: In youth he studied strenuously, mastered charts and chronicles comprehensively, was dull outwardly but bright within, and did not meddle with the age.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied hard and mastered historical and geographical texts; outwardly unassuming but inwardly sharp, he kept aloof from worldly entanglements.

sentences.zh: 年既長，始以仕家推蔭為興寧陵丞，調大理丞。

translations.literal: When he had grown older he first entered office through yin privilege as an official family and was made Assistant of Xingning Mausoleum, then transferred to Assistant in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Only in maturity did he enter office through family privilege as assistant at the Xingning imperial tomb, then was transferred to assistant in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 邊將蕭克濟督役苛暴，役者有醜言，有司以大逆論，遵慶曰：「財不足聚人，力不足加眾，焉能反？

translations.literal: The frontier general Xiao Keji supervised labor with harsh cruelty; the laborers spoke ugly words; the authorities judged it as great treason; Zunqing said: "Without wealth one cannot gather men, without strength one cannot overcome the multitude—how could they rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: The frontier general Xiao Keji drove corvée labor with brutal severity; when the laborers spoke rebelliously the authorities charged them with treason; Zunqing said, "Without wealth you cannot rally men, without power you cannot overcome the multitude—how could they rebel?"

sentences.zh: 」由是全救數十族。

translations.literal: " By this he wholly saved several tens of clans.
translations.idiomatic: " By this argument he saved dozens of families from execution.

sentences.zh: 頻擢吏部員外郎，判南曹。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Outer Director in the Ministry of Personnel and judged the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to outer director in the Ministry of Personnel with charge of the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 天寶時，選者歲萬計，遵慶性強敏，視簿牒，詳而不苛，世稱吏事第一。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era candidates each year numbered in the tens of thousands; Zunqing was by nature forceful and keen; in viewing registers he was thorough without harshness—the age called him first in clerical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era annual selections ran to ten thousand candidates; Zunqing was forceful and quick-witted, thorough but not harsh in reviewing records, and his contemporaries ranked him first in administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In Emperor Suzong's time he was Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Suzong he served as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 蕭華輔政，屢薦之，拜黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Xiao Hua assisted in government and repeatedly recommended him; he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Hua held power he recommended Zunqing repeatedly; Zunqing was appointed vice director of the Palace Secretariat and associate director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 代宗初，仆固懷恩反，帝以遵慶忠厚大臣，故奉詔宣慰，懷恩聽命將入朝，既而為其將范志誠沮止。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Daizong's reign Pugu Huai'en rebelled; the emperor, because Zunqing was a loyal and sincere great minister, therefore ordered him on edict to proclaim consolation; Huai'en obeyed and was about to enter court, but was then stopped by his general Fan Zhicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Daizong's reign Pugu Huai'en rebelled; the emperor sent the loyal and seasoned Zunqing on an edict of reassurance; Huai'en agreed to come to court but was then blocked by his general Fan Zhicheng.

sentences.zh: 時帝在陜，遵慶脫身赴行在。

translations.literal: The emperor was then at Shan; Zunqing escaped and hurried to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Shan; Zunqing broke free and made his way to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 帝還，遷太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, Zunqing was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned, Zunqing was made junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 罷為集賢院待制，改吏部尚書，以尚書右僕射復知選事，朝廷優其老，聽就第註官，時以為榮。

translations.literal: He was removed and made Attendant Drafting at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then changed to Minister of Personnel; as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat he again took charge of selection; the court favored his age and permitted him to register appointments at his mansion—at the time this was considered an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed to attendant drafting at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then made minister of personnel; as right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat he again oversaw civil-service selection; the court indulged his age and allowed him to register appointments from home—a mark of honor at the time.

sentences.zh: 嘗有族子病狂易，告以謀反，帝識其謬，置不問。

translations.literal: Once a clansman by marriage was ill with mania and reported that Zunqing was plotting rebellion; the emperor recognized the absurdity and set the matter aside.
translations.idiomatic: Once a kinsman by marriage, deranged by illness, accused him of plotting rebellion; the emperor saw through the charge and ignored it.

sentences.zh: 性惇正，老而彌謹。

translations.literal: By nature he was sincere and upright, and in old age grew all the more cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Sincere and upright by nature, he grew only more careful in old age.

sentences.zh: 每薦賢，有來謝者，以為恥。

translations.literal: Whenever he recommended the worthy, if anyone came to thank him he took it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he recommended a worthy man, he felt ashamed if the man came to thank him.

sentences.zh: 諫而見從，即內益畏。

translations.literal: When he remonstrated and was obeyed, inwardly he grew all the more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor accepted his remonstrance, he grew only more inwardly wary.

sentences.zh: 雖親近，但記其削稿疏數，而莫知所言。

translations.literal: Even those close to him only noted how many draft memorials he struck out, and did not know what he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Even his intimates knew only how many draft memorials he revised, not what they contained.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年薨，年九十餘。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dali he died, aged over ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Dali at more than ninety years of age.

sentences.zh: 初為郎時，著《王政記》，述今古治體，識者知其有公輔器云。

translations.literal: When he first served as a Gentleman he wrote Records of Royal Government, setting forth the governing structures of past and present; those who understood knew he had the capacity of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career as a court gentleman he wrote Records of Royal Government, surveying the principles of government ancient and modern; discerning readers saw in it the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 子向。

translations.literal: His son was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 向字傃仁，以蔭得調。

translations.literal: Xiang, styled Suren, entered office through yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, courtesy name Suren, entered office through family privilege.

sentences.zh: 建中初，李紓為同州刺史，奏署判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era Li Shu was Prefect of Tongzhou and memorialized to appoint him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong era Li Shu, as prefect of Tongzhou, had him appointed administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 李懷光叛河中，使其將趙貴先築壘於同州，紓奔奉天，而向領州務。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong and sent his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tongzhou; Shu fled to Fengtian, while Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong he sent his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tongzhou; Shu fled to Fengtian while Xiang remained to run the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貴先脅吏督役，不及期，將斬以徇，民皆駭散，向獨詣貴先壘開諭之，貴先乃降。

translations.literal: Guixian coerced clerks to drive labor; when the deadline was not met he was about to behead someone as an example; the people were all terrified and scattered; Xiang alone went to Guixian's camp and persuaded him openly; Guixian thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guixian forced officials to drive the labor gangs; when they missed the deadline he was about to execute someone as an example and the people fled in panic; Xiang alone went to Guixian's camp and talked him down, and Guixian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 同州不陷，向力也。

translations.literal: That Tongzhou did not fall was Xiang's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou did not fall—and that was Xiang's doing.

sentences.zh: 累為櫟陽、渭南令，奏課皆第一，擢戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served repeatedly as Magistrate of Liyang and Weinan; in memorial assessments he was always first and was promoted to Outer Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Liyang and Weinan, ranked first in every performance review, and was promoted to outer director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 德宗末，方鎮之副，多自選於朝，以待有變，次授之，故向以選為太原少尹、行軍司馬，歷陜虢觀察使，以吏部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Dezong's reign deputies of regional commands were mostly chosen from the court and held in reserve against change, then assigned in turn; thus Xiang through selection became Junior Administrator of Taiyuan and Marching Major, served as Investigating Commissioner of Shan-Guo, and retired as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Dezong's reign deputies for the regional commands were often chosen at court and held in reserve until needed; Xiang was thus selected as junior administrator of Taiyuan and marching major, later served as investigating commissioner of Shan-Guo, and retired as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 向能以學行持門戶，內外親屬百餘口，祿俸必均，世稱其孝睦。

translations.literal: Xiang was able through learning and conduct to uphold the household; within and without, kin numbered more than a hundred mouths, and salaries and stipends were always divided equally—the age praised his filial harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang upheld his house through learning and moral conduct; more than a hundred kin inside and outside the family shared his income equally, and his age praised his filial harmony.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died at eighty and was posthumously given Junior Guardian to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty and was posthumously honored as junior guardian to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 子寅，官累御史大夫。

translations.literal: His son was Yin, who rose through offices to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin rose to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 寅子樞。

translations.literal: Yin's son was Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son was Shu.

sentences.zh: 樞字紀聖，咸通中，第進士。

translations.literal: Shu, styled Jisheng, in the Xiantong era passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, courtesy name Jisheng, passed the jinshi examination during the Xiantong reign.

sentences.zh: 杜審權鎮河中，奏署幕府，再遷藍田尉。

translations.literal: When Du Shenquan governed Hezhong he memorialized to appoint him to the staff; he was twice promoted to Wei of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Shenquan governed Hezhong he had Shu join his staff; Shu was twice promoted to magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 宰相王鐸知之，遂直弘文館。

translations.literal: The chancellor Wang Duo knew of him and had him posted directly to the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor Wang Duo took notice of him and had him posted to the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 鐸罷，樞久不調。

translations.literal: When Duo was dismissed, Shu long went without reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: After Duo left office, Shu went long without a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 從僖宗入蜀，擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xizong into Shu and was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xizong into Shu and was promoted to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 中和初，鐸為都統，表署鄭滑掌書記。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhonghe era Duo was Commander-in-Chief and memorialized to appoint him as Secretary in Charge of Documents for Zheng-Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhonghe era, when Duo was commander-in-chief, he appointed Shu secretary in charge of documents for Zheng-Hua.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，進給事中，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Longji era he was advanced to Drafting Attendant and changed to Prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longji era he was promoted to drafting attendant and made prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 與孔緯厚善，緯以罪貶，故樞改右庶子，出為歙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was on close terms with Kong Wei; when Wei was demoted for guilt, Shu was therefore changed to Right Subordinate of the Heir and sent out as Prefect of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Kong Wei; when Wei was demoted for a crime, Shu was shifted to right subordinate of the heir and sent out as prefect of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 遷右散騎常侍，為汴州宣諭使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Regular Attendant of the Imperial Stud and made Proclaiming and Consoling Commissioner for Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right regular attendant of the imperial stud and made proclaiming and consoling commissioner for Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 樞素與朱全忠相結納，故全忠聽命，修貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: Shu had long been bound in alliance with Zhu Quanzhong, so Quanzhong obeyed orders and ceaselessly sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had long been allied with Zhu Quanzhong, who therefore obeyed the court and kept tribute flowing without interruption.

sentences.zh: 昭宗悅，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was pleased and promoted him to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong was pleased and promoted him to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時崔胤亦倚全忠專朝柄，因與樞善。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Yin also relied on Quanzhong to monopolize court power, and therefore was on good terms with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin then also relied on Quanzhong to dominate the court, and he and Shu were on good terms.

sentences.zh: 俄以戶部侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made vice minister of revenue and associate director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 帝在鳳翔，貶胤官，樞亦罷為工部尚書。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Fengxiang, Yin was demoted in rank and Shu was also removed, becoming Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Fengxiang, Yin was demoted and Shu was dismissed to the post of minister of works.

sentences.zh: 已還宮，拜檢校尚書右仆射、同平章事。

translations.literal: After returning to the palace he was appointed Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to the palace, Shu was appointed acting right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat and associate director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 出為清海節度使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as military commissioner of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military commissioner of Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 全忠言樞有經世才，不宜棄外，復拜門下侍郎平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: Quanzhong said Shu had talent to order the age and should not be abandoned in the outer circuits; he was again appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Director, with charge of compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong argued that Shu had the talent to govern the age and should not be cast out to the provinces; he was recalled as vice director of the Chancellery and associate director, with charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 累進右僕射、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to Right Vice Director and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport in all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to right vice director and commissioner for salt and iron transport in all circuits.

sentences.zh: 哀帝嗣位，柳璨方用事，全忠以牙將張廷範為太常卿，樞以為廷範勛臣，自宜任方鎮，何用為卿，恐非王意，持不下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aidi succeeded, Liu Can was just then in power; Quanzhong wished to make his military officer Zhang Tingfan Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Shu held that Tingfan was a meritorious minister and ought to be assigned to a regional command—what use was there in making him Director? He feared this was not the king's intent and withheld approval.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aidi succeeded, Liu Can was in power; Quanzhong wanted his officer Zhang Tingfan made director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Shu argued that a meritorious general belonged in the regions, not in such a court post, and fearing this was not the emperor's wish, he withheld approval.

sentences.zh: 全忠怒謂賓佐曰：「吾常器樞不浮薄，今乃爾。

translations.literal: Quanzhong angrily told his guests and aides: "I always valued Shu as not shallow or frivolous—now he is like this."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong angrily told his staff, "I always thought Shu was no lightweight—now look at him."

sentences.zh: 」璨聞，即罷樞政事，拜左僕射。

translations.literal: " When Can heard, he at once removed Shu from government affairs and appointed him Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: " When Can heard, he immediately stripped Shu of his political duties and named him left vice director.

sentences.zh: 俄貶登州刺史，又貶瀧州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was demoted to Prefect of Dengzhou, then again demoted to Revenue Aide of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted to prefect of Dengzhou, then again to revenue aide of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 至滑州，全忠遣人殺之白馬驛，投屍於河，年六十五。

translations.literal: When he reached Huazhou, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post Station and cast his body into the river; he was sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: At Huazhou, Quanzhong had him killed at Baima Post Station and his body thrown into the river; he was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 初，全忠佐吏李振曰：「此等自謂清流，宜投諸訶，永為濁流。

translations.literal: At first Quanzhong's aide Li Zhen said: "These men call themselves the clear current—they ought to be cast into the He, forever to be the muddy current."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Quanzhong's aide Li Zhen had said, "These men call themselves the pure stream—they ought to be thrown into the Yellow River and become the muddy stream forever."

sentences.zh: 」全忠笑而許之。

translations.literal: " Quanzhong laughed and consented.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong laughed and agreed.

sentences.zh: 呂諲，河中河東人。

translations.literal: Lü Yin, a native of Hedong in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yin was from Hedong in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少力於學，志行整飭。

translations.literal: In youth he strove in study; his aims and conduct were orderly and disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied hard; his aims and conduct were disciplined and upright.

sentences.zh: 孤貧不自業，裏人程氏財雄於鄉，以女妻諲，亦以諲才不久困，厚分貲贍濟所欲，故稱譽日廣。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor, he could not establish himself; a village man of the Cheng clan was wealthy and powerful in the district; he gave his daughter in marriage to Yin, also thinking that Yin's talent would not long remain in hardship; he generously divided wealth to supply what Yin desired, and so Yin's reputation daily spread.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he could not support himself; a wealthy local man of the Cheng clan gave him his daughter in marriage, believing Yin's talent would not long go unrewarded, and generously supplied his needs, so Yin's reputation steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 開元末，入京師，第進士，調寧陵尉，采訪使韋陟署為支使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he entered the capital, passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Wei of Ningling, and Investigating Commissioner Wei Zhi appointed him as branch commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Kaiyuan reign he went to the capital, passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Ningling, and was made branch commissioner by the investigating commissioner Wei Zhi.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰節度河西，表支度判官。

translations.literal: Geshu Han governed Hexi as military commissioner and memorialized to appoint him as administrative aide for expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: When Geshu Han was military commissioner of Hexi he had Yin appointed administrative aide for expenditures.

sentences.zh: 歷太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Master of Ceremonies to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant master of ceremonies to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 性靜慎，勤總吏職，諸僚或出遊，諲獨頹然據案，鉤視簿最，翰益親之。

translations.literal: By nature he was quiet and cautious, diligent in overseeing clerical duties; when fellow officials went out on pleasure outings Yin alone sat bowed over his desk, checking and surveying registers; Han grew all the more intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and cautious by nature, he was diligent in administrative work; while colleagues went out on pleasure outings Yin alone bent over his desk auditing the records, and Han grew all the closer to him.

sentences.zh: 累兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He cumulatively served as Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He also served cumulatively as palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 翰敗潼關，諲西趨靈武，由中人尉薦，肅宗才之，拜御史中丞，所陳事無不順納。

translations.literal: When Han was defeated at Tong Pass, Yin hurried west to Lingwu; through recommendation by the eunuch Wei, Emperor Suzong recognized his talent and appointed him Censor-in-Chief; whatever he presented was without exception accepted.
translations.idiomatic: After Han's defeat at Tong Pass, Yin hurried west to Lingwu; recommended by the eunuch Wei, Emperor Suzong recognized his ability and made him censor-in-chief; everything he proposed was accepted.

sentences.zh: 從至鳳翔，遷武部侍郎。

translations.literal: He followed on to Fengxiang and was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the court to Fengxiang and was made vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 帝復兩京，詔盡系群臣之汙賊者，以御史中丞崔器、憲部侍郎韓擇木、大理卿嚴向為三司使處其罪，又詔御史大夫李峴及諲領使。

translations.literal: When the emperor recovered the two capitals, an edict ordered that all officials who had defiled themselves by serving the rebels be imprisoned; Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi, Vice Minister of Justice Han Zemu, and Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review Yan Xiang were made the Three Offices commissioners to dispose of their crimes; another edict ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Xian and Yin to head the commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were recovered, an edict ordered all officials who had served the rebels imprisoned; Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi, Vice Minister of Justice Han Zemu, and chief justice Yan Xiang were made commissioners of the Three Offices to judge their crimes; another edict named Censor-in-Chief Li Xian and Yin to lead the commission.

sentences.zh: 諲於權宜知大體不及峴，而援律傅經過之，當時憚其持法，然以峴故，多所平反。

translations.literal: Yin in expedient policy and grasp of great principles did not match Xian, yet in citing law and applying the classics he went too far; at the time people feared his enforcement of law, yet because of Xian many cases were reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was less adept than Xian at flexible policy and the larger view, but he applied the law and the classics with excessive rigor; contemporaries feared his severity, yet thanks to Xian many verdicts were overturned.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，九節度兵敗，帝憂之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan the armies of the nine military commissioners were defeated; the emperor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyuan the armies of the nine commissioners were defeated, and the emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 擢諲同中書門下平章事，知門下省，翌日，復以李峴、李揆、第五琦為宰相，而苗晉卿、王玙罷。

translations.literal: Yin was promoted to Associate Director of the Chancellery with charge of the Chancellery office; the next day Li Xian, Li Kui, and Diwu Qi were again made chancellors, while Miao Jinqing and Wang Yu were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was promoted to associate director of the Chancellery with charge of the Chancellery office; the next day Li Xian, Li Kui, and Diwu Qi were again made chancellors, while Miao Jinqing and Wang Yu were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 會母喪解，三月復召知門下省事，兼判度支，還執政。

translations.literal: He met his mother's mourning and resigned; after three months he was again summoned to oversee Chancellery affairs, concurrently judging the Department of Public Works, and returned to government.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on his mother's death; three months later he was recalled to oversee Chancellery affairs and concurrently to judge the Department of Public Works, and returned to power.

sentences.zh: 累封須昌縣伯，遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Baron of Xuchang county and transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Xuchang and promoted to vice director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上元初，加同中書門下三品，當賜門戟，或勸諲以兇服受吉賜不宜，諲釋缞拜賜，人譏其失禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan he was given the rank of Third Grade Associate Director of the Chancellery; when he was to be granted halberds for his gate, some urged Yin that in mourning garb it was unfitting to receive an auspicious gift; Yin removed his hemp mourning and bowed to receive the gift—people mocked his breach of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shangyuan era he was raised to third-grade associate director of the Chancellery; when court halberds were to be bestowed, some urged that accepting such an honor in mourning dress was improper; Yin removed his mourning garments and bowed to receive them, and people mocked the breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 諲引妻之父楚賓為衛尉少卿，楚賓子震為郎官。

translations.literal: Yin brought in his wife's father Chubin as Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Chubin's son Zhen became a Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yin installed his father-in-law Chubin as vice director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Chubin's son Zhen as a palace gentleman.

sentences.zh: 中人馬尚言者，素匿於諲，為人求官，諲奏為藍田尉。

translations.literal: The eunuch Ma Shangyan had long been sheltered by Yin; he sought office for others and Yin memorialized to make him Wei of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Ma Shangyan, whom Yin had long sheltered, solicited offices for others; Yin memorialized to make him magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 事覺，帝怒，命敬羽窮治，殺尚言，以其肉賜從官，罷諲為太子賓客。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed the emperor was angry, ordered Jing Yu to investigate to the end, executed Shangyan, gave his flesh to attendant officials as a gift, and dismissed Yin to Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light the emperor was furious, ordered Jing Yu to investigate thoroughly, executed Shangyan and had his flesh given to attending officials, and demoted Yin to guest of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 數月，拜荊州長史、澧朗峽忠等五州節度使。

translations.literal: After several months he was appointed Chief Administrator of Jingzhou and military commissioner of the five prefectures of Li, Lang, Xia, Zhong, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was appointed chief administrator of Jingzhou and military commissioner over five prefectures including Li, Lang, Xia, and Zhong.

sentences.zh: 諲始建請荊州置南都，詔可。

translations.literal: Yin was the first to propose establishing a Southern Capital at Jingzhou; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was the first to propose making Jingzhou a southern capital; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 於是更號江陵府，以諲為尹，置永平軍萬人，遏吳、蜀之沖，以湖南之嶽、潭、郴、道、邵、連，黔中之涪凡七州，隸其道。

translations.literal: Thereupon the name was changed to Jiangling Prefecture; Yin was made Prefect; the Yongping Army of ten thousand men was established to block the thrust of Wu and Shu; the seven prefectures of Yue, Tan, Chen, Dao, Shao, and Lian in Hunan, and Fu in Qianzhong, were placed under his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The district was then renamed Jiangling prefecture with Yin as prefect; a Yongping army of ten thousand men was established to guard the route between Wu and Shu; seven prefectures in Hunan and Fu in Qianzhong were placed under his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 初，荊州長史張惟一以衡州蠻酋陳希昂為司馬，督家兵千人自防，惟一親將牟遂金與相忤，希昂率兵至惟一所捕之，惟一懼，斬其首以謝，悉以遂金兵屬之，乃退，自是政一出希昂，後入朝，遷常州刺史，過江陵入謁，諲伏甲擊殺之，誅黨偶數十人，積屍府門，內外震服。

translations.literal: At first Chief Administrator Zhang Weiyi of Jingzhou made the Man chieftain of Hengzhou, Chen Xi'ang, his Major, supervising a thousand household troops for self-defense; Weiyi's close general Mou Suijin quarreled with him; Xi'ang led troops to Weiyi's place and seized him; Weiyi was afraid, beheaded Suijin's head to apologize, and turned all of Suijin's troops over to him, then withdrew; from this government issued entirely from Xi'ang; later he entered court and was transferred to Prefect of Changzhou; passing Jiangling he entered to pay respects; Yin set armed men in ambush and killed him, executed several tens of his party and associates, heaped corpses at the prefectural gate, and within and without were shaken into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chief Administrator Zhang Weiyi of Jingzhou had made the Hengzhou Man chieftain Chen Xi'ang his major with a thousand household troops for defense; Weiyi's officer Mou Suijin quarreled with Xi'ang, who marched on Weiyi's headquarters and seized him; Weiyi, in fear, beheaded Suijin to appease Xi'ang and handed over all his troops, after which Xi'ang controlled the prefecture; later Xi'ang went to court and was made prefect of Changzhou; passing Jiangling he paid a courtesy call; Yin set an ambush and killed him, executed dozens of his followers, and piled the bodies at the prefectural gate until the region was cowed into submission.

sentences.zh: 妖人申泰芝用左道事李輔國，擢諫議大夫，置軍邵、道二州間，以泰芝總之，納群蠻金，賞以緋紫，出褚中詔書賜衣示之，群蠻怵於賞，而財不足，更為剽掠，吏不敢制。

translations.literal: The sorcerer Shen Taizhi used heterodox ways to serve Li Fuguo and was promoted to Remonstrance Grand Master; armies were placed between Shao and Dao prefectures with Taizhi in overall command; he collected gold from the various Man tribes, rewarded them with crimson and purple, produced imperial edicts from his pouch to bestow robes and show them; the Man tribes were cowed by rewards yet their wealth was insufficient, and they turned again to plunder—officials did not dare restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer Shen Taizhi practiced heterodox rites in Li Fuguo's service and was made remonstrance grand master; troops were stationed between Shao and Dao with Taizhi in command; he extorted gold from the Man tribes, rewarded them with crimson and purple robes, and produced edicts from his pouch to prove imperial favor; tempted by rewards but still poor, the tribes turned again to raiding, and officials dared not stop them.

sentences.zh: 潭州刺史龐承鼎疾其奸，因泰芝過潭，縛付吏，劾贓鉅萬，得左道讖記，並奏之。

translations.literal: Pang Chengdong, Prefect of Tanzhou, hated his wickedness; when Taizhi passed through Tan he bound him and handed him to the authorities, impeached him for bribes of tens of thousands, obtained heterodox prognostic writings, and memorialized all together.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhou prefect Pang Chengdong detested his crimes; when Taizhi passed through Tan he had him bound and handed over to the authorities, impeached him for bribes in the tens of thousands, seized heterodox prophetic writings, and memorialized the whole case.

sentences.zh: 輔國矯追泰芝還京，既召見，反譖承鼎陷不辜，詔諲按罪。

translations.literal: Fuguo forged an order recalling Taizhi to the capital; after he was received in audience he in turn slandered Chengdong for framing the innocent; an edict ordered Yin to investigate the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo forged a recall bringing Taizhi to the capital; after an audience Taizhi slandered Chengdong for framing an innocent man, and an edict ordered Yin to investigate.

sentences.zh: 諲使判官嚴郢具獄，暴泰芝惡。

translations.literal: Yin sent his administrative aide Yan Ying to complete the dossier, exposing Taizhi's evils.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent his aide Yan Ying to compile the case and expose Taizhi's crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝不省，賜承鼎死，流郢建州。

translations.literal: The emperor did not understand; he granted Chengdong death and exiled Ying to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen; Chengdong was sentenced to death and Ying exiled to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 後泰芝終以贓徙死，承鼎追原其誣。

translations.literal: Later Taizhi in the end died in exile for bribery; Chengdong was posthumously cleared of the false charge.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhi later died in exile for corruption; Chengdong was posthumously cleared of the false charge.

sentences.zh: 諲為治，不急細務，決大事剛果不撓。

translations.literal: In governing, Yin did not press petty affairs; in deciding great matters he was firm and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: In administration Yin did not fuss over small matters, but in great decisions he was firm and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 始在河西，悉知諸將能否，及為尹，奏取材者數十人總牙兵，故威惠兩行。

translations.literal: When he was first in Hexi he fully knew which generals could or could not perform; when he became Prefect he memorialized to select several tens of able men to command the guard troops, and so both awe and kindness were exercised.
translations.idiomatic: In Hexi he had learned which generals were capable; as prefect he selected dozens of able men to command the guard troops, and so combined authority with kindness.

sentences.zh: 諲之相，與李揆不平，既斥，乃用善治聞。

translations.literal: When Yin was chancellor he was at odds with Li Kui; once dismissed, he became known for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor he had been at odds with Li Kui; after his dismissal he won renown for effective rule.

sentences.zh: 揆恐帝復用，即妄奏置軍湖南非便，又陰遣人刺諲過失。

translations.literal: Kui feared the emperor would reuse him and at once falsely memorialized that establishing armies in Hunan was inconvenient, and also secretly sent men to probe Yin's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, fearing the emperor might recall him, falsely memorialized that stationing troops in Hunan was imprudent and secretly sent men to dig up Yin's faults.

sentences.zh: 諲上疏訟其事，帝怒，逐揆出之，顯條其罪。

translations.literal: Yin submitted a memorial pleading the matter; the emperor was angry, drove Kui out, and openly listed his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yin memorialized to expose the plot; the emperor was furious, expelled Kui, and publicly listed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 諲苦羸疾，卒，年五十一，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Yin suffered from wasting illness and died, aged fifty-one; posthumously he was given Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Worn down by illness, Yin died at fifty-one and was posthumously honored as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 諲在朝不稱任職相，及為荊州，號令明，賦斂均一。

translations.literal: Yin in court did not fit the role of chancellor; when he was at Jingzhou his orders were clear and tax levies uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Yin did not distinguish himself as chancellor at court, but as prefect of Jingzhou his orders were clear and his taxes even-handed.

sentences.zh: 其治尚威信，故軍士用命，闔境無盜賊，民歌詠之。

translations.literal: His governance valued authority and trust, so soldiers obeyed orders, the whole territory had no bandits or thieves, and the people sang praises of him.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled through authority and trust; the troops obeyed, banditry vanished throughout the region, and the people sang his praise.

sentences.zh: 自至德以來，處方面數十人，諲最有名。

translations.literal: From Zhide onward, of the several tens who held regional commands, Yin was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhide era onward, among dozens who held regional commands, none was more celebrated than Yin.

sentences.zh: 荊人生構房祠，及歿，吏裒錢十萬徙祠府西。

translations.literal: The people of Jing on their own built a hall-shrine to him; when he died, officials collected a hundred thousand in cash and moved the shrine west of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jing built a shrine to him on their own initiative; after his death officials raised a hundred thousand cash and moved the shrine to the west of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 始，諲知杜鴻漸、元載才，薦於朝，後皆為宰相。

translations.literal: At the beginning Yin recognized the talent of Du Hongjian and Yuan Zai and recommended them to court; both later became chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Yin recognized the talents of Du Hongjian and Yuan Zai and recommended them to court; both later became chancellors.

sentences.zh: 永泰中，嚴郢以故吏請謚有司，博士獨孤及謚曰「肅」，郢以故事宰相謚皆二名，請益曰「忠肅」。

translations.literal: In the Yongtai era Yan Ying, as a former subordinate, requested a posthumous title from the authorities; the Erudite Dugu Ji gave the title Su; Ying, citing precedent that chancellors' posthumous titles were always two characters, requested that it be augmented to Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongtai era Yan Ying, as a former subordinate, petitioned the authorities for a posthumous title; the erudite Dugu Ji proposed Su; Ying, citing precedent that chancellors received two-character posthumous titles, asked that it be expanded to Zhongsu.

sentences.zh: 及執奏，謂：「謚在義美惡，不在多名。

translations.literal: When he presented the memorial he said: "Posthumous titles lie in praising good and condemning evil, not in many names.
translations.idiomatic: When he presented the memorial he argued, "A posthumous title lies in praising virtue and condemning vice, not in multiplying names.

sentences.zh: 文王伐崇，周公殺三監、淮夷，重耳一戰而霸，而謚曰文。

translations.literal: King Wen attacked Chong, the Duke of Zhou killed the Three Overseers and the Huaiyi, Chong'er with one battle became hegemon—yet their posthumous titles were Wen.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen attacked Chong, the Duke of Zhou executed the Three Overseers and the Huaiyi, and Chong'er became hegemon after a single battle—yet all were posthumously titled Wen.

sentences.zh: 冀缺之恪，寧俞之忠，隨會不忘其君，而謚曰武。

translations.literal: Ji Que's reverence, Ning Yu's loyalty, Sui Hui's not forgetting his lord—yet their posthumous titles were Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Que was reverent, Ning Yu loyal, and Sui Hui never forgot his lord—yet they were posthumously titled Wu.

sentences.zh: 故知稱其大、略其細也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that the great is named and the small is passed over.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that a title names what is great and passes over what is small.

sentences.zh: 且二名謚，非古也。

translations.literal: Moreover two-character posthumous titles are not ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, two-character posthumous titles are not ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 漢興，蕭何、張良、霍去病、霍光以文武大略，佐漢致太平，一名不盡其善，乃有文終、文成、景桓、宣成之謚。

translations.literal: When Han arose, Xiao He, Zhang Liang, Huo Qubing, and Huo Guang with civil and military grand strategies assisted Han to great peace; one name could not exhaust their goodness, and so there were the posthumous titles Wenzong, Wencheng, Jinghuan, and Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han arose, Xiao He, Zhang Liang, Huo Qubing, and Huo Guang, with grand civil and military designs, helped bring the dynasty to peace; a single character could not exhaust their merit, and so they received compound titles such as Wenzong, Wencheng, Jinghuan, and Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 唐興，參用漢制，魏徵以王道佐時近『文』，愛君忘身近『貞』，二者並優，廢一莫可，故曰文貞。

translations.literal: When Tang arose it adopted the Han system; Wei Zheng with the kingly way assisting the age was close to "Wen," loving the lord and forgetting the self was close to "Zhen"—both excellences together, abandoning one was impossible, and so it was called Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang arose it followed the Han model: Wei Zheng's kingly service to the age approached Wen, and his love of the ruler at the cost of self approached Zhen; both virtues were outstanding and neither could be dropped, hence Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀端直近『貞』，性多猜近『褊』，言『褊』則失『貞』，稱『貞』則遺『褊』，故曰貞褊。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu's uprightness was close to "Zhen," his nature much given to suspicion was close to "Pian"—to say "Pian" would lose "Zhen," to call "Zhen" would omit "Pian"—and so it was called Zhenpian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu's uprightness approached Zhen, but his suspicious nature approached Pian; to say Pian would lose Zhen, to say Zhen would omit Pian—hence Zhenpian.

sentences.zh: 蓋有為為之也。

translations.literal: These were all done with deliberate purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Such cases were deliberate exceptions.

sentences.zh: 若跡無異稱，則易以一字。

translations.literal: If the record had no exceptional designation, then a single character would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Where the record offered nothing exceptional, a single character was enough.

sentences.zh: 故杜如晦曰成，封德彜曰明，王珪曰懿，陳叔達曰忠，溫彥博曰恭，岑文本曰憲，韋世源曰昭，皆當時赫赫居宰相位者，謚不過一名。

translations.literal: Thus Du Ruhui was called Cheng, Feng Deyi Ming, Wang Gui Yi, Chen Shuda Zhong, Wen Yanbo Gong, Cen Wende Xian, Wei Shiyuan Zhao—all at the time illustrious in chancellor posts—yet their posthumous titles were no more than one name.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Du Ruhui was titled Cheng, Feng Deyi Ming, Wang Gui Yi, Chen Shuda Zhong, Wen Yanbo Gong, Cen Wende Xian, and Wei Shiyuan Zhao—all celebrated chancellors of their day—yet each received only a single-character posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 而言故事宰相必以二名，固所未聞。

translations.literal: Yet to say that by precedent chancellors must have two names is something never heard of.
translations.idiomatic: The claim that chancellors must by precedent receive two-character titles is something never heard of before.

sentences.zh: 宜如前謚。

translations.literal: It should follow the earlier posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier title should stand.

sentences.zh: 」遂不改。

translations.literal: " It was therefore not changed.
translations.idiomatic: " It was therefore not changed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：孔子稱才難。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Confucius called talent rare.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Confucius said that talent is hard to find.

sentences.zh: 然人之才有限，不得皆善。

translations.literal: Yet human talent has limits and cannot all be good.
translations.idiomatic: Yet human talent has its limits, and no one can excel in everything.

sentences.zh: 觀圓之銳，而失守出奔；

translations.literal: Consider Yuan's keenness, yet he lost his post and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan was sharp yet lost his command and fled;

sentences.zh: 晉卿雅厚，而少風采臧否；

translations.literal: Jinqing was refined and generous, yet lacked the spirit to judge right and wrong;
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jinqing was gracious and mild, yet lacked the force to judge right from wrong;

sentences.zh: 冕明強，嗜利不知大體；

translations.literal: Mian was bright and forceful, greedy for profit and ignorant of great principles;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian was capable and forceful, yet greedy and blind to larger duties;

sentences.zh: 諲輔政，功名不及治郡。

translations.literal: Yin assisted in government, yet his fame and achievement did not match his governing a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yin as chancellor achieved less than he did governing a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 然各以所長顯於時。

translations.literal: Yet each by his strength shone in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each made his particular strength count in his own day.

sentences.zh: 故聖人使人也器之，不窮所不能而後為治也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage in employing men treats them as vessels, not exhausting what they cannot do and only then governing.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sage employs men according to their capacities, not demanding what they cannot give, and only then achieves good government.

sentences.zh: 遵慶寡疵，中人之賢與。

translations.literal: Zunqing had few flaws—perhaps the worth of an average man.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing had few faults—perhaps the worth of a capable but unremarkable man.
